sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 246.

PD 246.

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 246 was established by Ordinance No. 19264, passed by the Dallas City Council on August 27, 1986. Ordinance No. 19264 amended Ordinance No. 10962, Chapter 51 of the Dallas City Code, as amended. (Ord. Nos. 10962; 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 246 is established on property generally located at the northeast corner of Dallas Parkway and Spring Valley Road. The size of PD 246 is approximately 4.98 acres. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(c) For purposes of this article, references to office use mean office, medical clinic, and bank or savings and loan office uses as defined in the Dallas Development Code unless otherwise stated. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Conceptual Site Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.104. CONCEPTUAL SITE PLAN.

Development of the Property must be in conformance with the conceptual site plan (Exhibit 246A). (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Land Use Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.105. LAND USE PLAN.

The Dallas Parkway Center Study is a land use study adopted by the city council on June 26, 1985, which addresses, among other things, problems of density and transportation in an area bounded by L.B.J. Freeway (I.H. 635), the Dallas North Tollway, Belt Line Road, and Montfort Road. A copy of the adopted study is on file in the department of development services. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Within one year of August 27, 1986, a detailed development plan for all or a portion of the Property must be submitted to the city plan commission for approval. A detailed development plan for the Property must be approved by the city plan commission prior to the issuance of any building permit on the Property. Detailed development plans covering only a portion of the Property are acceptable provided that no building permit is issued for a portion of the Property not covered by an approved detailed development plan. All detailed development plans must comply with the conceptual site plan. All detailed

development plans must include the site plan requisites listed in Section 51-4.803(d). In deciding whether to approve or deny the development plan, the city plan commission shall follow the standards set out for the director of development services in Section 51-4.803. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.107. USES.

The only uses permitted on the Property are those uses permitted in an SC Shopping Center District and multiple-family uses. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Landscape Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.108. LANDSCAPE PLAN.

A landscape plan must be submitted with each detailed development plan and must be approved by the city plan commission prior to the issuance of any building permit on the portion of the Property included in the corresponding detailed development plan. The landscaping must be installed in accordance with the landscape plan within six months of the issuance of any certificate of occupancy on the portion of the Property included in the corresponding detailed development plan. All plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition at all times. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Height And Setbacks
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.109. HEIGHT AND SETBACKS.

Minimum setbacks and maximum heights for all structures on the Property are as indicated on the conceptual site plan. Any building height that exceeds 173 feet in height must be approved by the Federal Aviation Administration as not hazardous to air navigation prior to the issuance of a building permit for the building. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Lot Coverage
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.110. LOT COVERAGE.

Maximum permitted lot coverage of the Property, excluding above-grade parking structures, is 40 percent. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Floor Area
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.111. FLOOR AREA.

(a) Generally. Total permitted floor area for all nonresidential uses and hotel uses combined on the Property is 347,753 square feet. Total maximum permitted floor area by right in square feet ("sf") for certain uses are as follows:

(1) Hotel - 317,325 sf.

(2) Office - 284,723 sf.

(3) Retail, bar and restaurant uses (retail-related uses) - 32,602 sf.

(b) Special conversion provisions.

(1) In addition to the maximum permitted floor area for office use listed above, up to 10,867 square feet of the permitted retail-related use floor area may be converted to office use floor area at a ratio of one square foot of retail to two square feet of office use, to a maximum of 21,735 square feet of additional office use.

(2) In addition to the maximum office floor area listed above, hotel floor area may be converted to office use floor area at a ratio of three square feet of hotel floor area to one square foot of office use floor area, to a maximum of 10,143 square feet of additional office use.

(3) If all of both the retail-related and hotel floor area are converted to office uses, a maximum of 316,601 square feet of office use is permitted. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.112. OFF-STREET PARKING.

(a) Phased office parking limit. In order to promote the development of transportation alternatives, the maximum number of parking spaces for office uses on the Property is restricted in accordance with the regulations below. In order to permit adequate parking for initial phases of development, the restrictions are phased in to gradually reduce the ratio of parking spaces to office floor area from 3.0 spaces for each 1,000 square feet of floor area to 2.38 for each 1,000 square feet of floor area as development progresses. For the purpose of this phased office parking limit and minimum office parking, "office use" does not include medical clinics.

(1) Maximum number of parking spaces for office use is 3.0 spaces per 1,000 square feet of floor area until building permits have been issued for construction of 217,346 or more square feet of floor area of office use.

(2) When building permits have been issued for construction of more than 217,346 but less than 271,682 square feet of floor area of office use, the maximum number of parking spaces is 2.5 spaces per 1,000 square feet of office use.

(3) When building permits have been issued for construction of more than 271,682 square feet of floor area of office use, the maximum number of parking spaces for office use is 2.38 spaces per 1,000 square feet of floor area.

(b) Minimum office parking. Minimum permissible number of parking spaces provided for office use at any stage of development is 2.0 spaces per 1,000 square feet of floor area.

(c) Requirements for other uses. All uses other than office must supply parking in compliance with the minimum requirements of the Dallas Development Code; however, no off-street parking may be supplied in excess of the code requirement. The provisions of Section 51-4.301(c)(6) (the mixed use parking reduction bonus) do not act to restrict the maximum number of spaces permitted, but may be used to calculate the minimum number of spaces permitted.

(d) No parking signs. The owner(s) of the Property must fund the posting of no-parking signs on all dedicated streets traversing and bordering the Property, at the direction of the director of the department of public works and transportation. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Vehicular Access
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.113. VEHICULAR ACCESS.

Curb cuts for vehicular ingress-egress to and from the Property are limited to the number and approximate locations shown on the conceptual site plan. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Road Improvements
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.114. ROAD IMPROVEMENTS.

(a) Dedications. The owner(s) of the Property must dedicate all rights-of-way and easements indicated on the conceptual site plan within ninety days of receiving notice from the director of public works and transportation or his designee that the city is preparing to begin paving operations on that road, or prior to applying for any building permit, whichever comes first. A dedication fulfills the requirements of this section if it is an easement for street and utility purposes or a greater estate in real property.

(b) On-site improvements.

(1) The owner(s) of the Property must fund paving and drainage improvements to the specifications of the department of public works and transportation for improvements to Spring Valley Road and the Dallas North Tollway service road along the Property frontage in accordance with the thoroughfare plan for these roads. Funding must be provided for each road improvement within 90 days of receiving notice from the director of public works and transportation or his designee that the city is prepared to begin paving operations for that road.

(2) The owner(s) of the Property must fund the full cost of any needed acceleration- deceleration lanes, as determined by the director of public works and transportation.

(c) Impact fee for off-site improvements. Prior to the issuance of any building permit for construction of a building for office use, the owner(s) must pay a fee of $.50 per square foot of floor area of office use for which a building permit is sought. This fee shall be adjusted annually, using 1986 as the base year, by the director of public works and transportation to account for increases in the cost of eight- inch thick, 3,000 psi reinforced Portland cement concrete pavement. The fees collected under this article must be:

(1) placed in separate interest-bearing accounts in the Dallas Parkway Center Thoroughfare Improvements Fund; and

(2) used for off-site road improvements, as defined in the Dallas Parkway Center Study on file with the department of development services.

(d) Credits. If a person finances directly any off-site road construction within the area defined in the Dallas Parkway Center Study, and if that financing has received prior written approval from the director of public works and transportation, he shall receive a credit for those construction costs. Included in this credit is the appraised value, or the acquisition cost, whichever is less, of off-site right-of- way conveyed to the city. The appraised value is to be determined by the director of development services as of the date of conveyance. Right-of-way that is within the boundaries of or contiguous to the Property is not off-site right-of-way. No credit given under this subsection may exceed the maximum fee required for full development of the Property under this article.

(e) Refund of fee. If, after a period of 10 years from the time of payment of a fee, any portion of the money has not been spent by transfer, allocation, or any other method, for the specified improvements based on a first-in/first-out accounting method, the remaining portion of the fee paid shall be refunded to the payor, or his assignee, with interest accrued at the city's investment rate, less administrative costs, upon his application for refund, which must include proof of the amount and time of payment.

(f) Replacement of fee. If an area-wide road improvement fee is established by the city, that fee shall replace the fee established in this article, and the portion of any fees already paid under this article in excess of the area-wide fee will be credited toward future payments upon proof of overpayment. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Paving
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.115. PAVING.

(a) All streets, driveways, parking spaces, and maneuvering areas for parking must comply with the requirements of the Dallas Development Code.

(b) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.116. SIGNS.

All signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts contained in Article VII; however, no non-premise signs are permitted. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Transportation System Management (Tsm)
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.117. TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM MANAGEMENT (TSM).

(a) General. The owner(s) of the Property shall establish and operate a TSM program to encourage carpool, vanpool, and other transit alternatives. A specific TSM action program must be submitted to the city plan commission within one year of August 27, 1986, or concurrent with the submission of the first detailed development plan, whichever is sooner.

(b) Reports. An annual report must be furnished to the director of public works and transportation for analysis and review. The first report must be submitted within two years after the issuance of the first certificate of occupancy on the Property and reports must be submitted annually thereafter until the director of public works and transportation otherwise directs. The final report must be submitted two years after the issuance of the certificate of occupancy which would permit occupancy of 90 percent of the final building shown on the detailed development plan(s).

(c) Alternative. In lieu of the requirements in Subsection (a), the owner(s) of the Property may participate in and fund on a pro rata basis with other local area property owners, and area-wide Transportation Management Organization (TMO) that is approved by the city. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Mandatory      Transportation                           Management
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.118. MANDATORY TRANSPORTATION MANAGEMENT ORGANIZATION (TMO) SUPPORT FEE.

(a) General. Prior to the issuance of any building permit for construction of a building for office use, the owner(s) must pay to the director of public works and transportation a fee of $.05 per square floor of office use for which a building permit is sought. The fees collected under this article must:

(i) be placed in separate interest-bearing accounts in a special fund; and

(ii) used for the establishment and operation of an area-wide TMO for the area described in the Dallas Parkway Center Study. The fee must be adjusted annually, using 1986 as the base year, by the director of public works and transportation to reflect changes in service costs by using the Consumer Price Index for Urban Consumers (CPIU) for the Dallas/Fort Worth Standard Metropolitan Statistical Area.

(b) Refund. If, after a period of five years from the time of a payment of a TMO fee, at least 80 percent of the interest earned for TMO operations, has not been spent by transfer, allocation, or any other method, based on a first-in/first-out accounting method, the fee paid must be refunded to the payor,

or his assignee, with any interest accrued at the city's investment rate, upon his application for refund, which must include proof of the amount and time of payment. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: General Requirements
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.119. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS.

(a) Development of Property must comply with the requirements of all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit or a certificate of occupancy for a use in this PD until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other applicable ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-246.120. ZONING MAP.

PD 246 is located on Zoning Map No. C-7. (Ord. Nos. 19264; 25711)
